module.title: Days 1–10 | Competition Mastery Module
module.description: Production candidate: authored topic-driven National Aptitude Championship curriculum.

lessons.title: Quantitative aptitude
lessons.objective: Build competition-ready understanding of quantitative aptitude and apply it accurately to unfamiliar questions.
lessons.core_teaching_content: Aptitude problems reward efficient setup, estimation and verification. Translate words into quantities or logical relationships before calculating. Percentages, rates, averages and mixtures require consistent units and careful interpretation of the base quantity. Data interpretation demands attention to axes, labels and totals. Under time pressure, estimate first, choose a sensible method, then verify whether the result is in a plausible range. In this lesson, focus specifically on quantitative aptitude. Identify the defining concepts, the distinctions that commonly cause mistakes, and the evidence or procedure needed to justify an answer. Practise moving from recognition to application: first identify what the question is testing, then select a method, perform the reasoning carefully, and verify the result against the wording and constraints. Keep an error log that records the misconception or decision error, not just the correct answer.
examples: A National Aptitude Championship question on quantitative aptitude should be solved by identifying the key clue, applying the relevant principle, and checking the option against all stated conditions.
Create a new quantitative aptitude scenario with one tempting distractor. Explain why the correct response is supported and why the distractor fails.
lessons.practical_activity: Complete a focused National Aptitude Championship activity on quantitative aptitude. Build a small table, diagram, worked example, speaking sample, writing sample or practice set as appropriate to the subject, then explain the reasoning behind the result.
lessons.guided_practice: Work through three scaffolded tasks on quantitative aptitude: model the first, prompt the second, and require independent justification on the third. Ask the learner to identify the exact clue, rule or evidence used before confirming the answer.
independent_practice: Solve three unfamiliar questions on quantitative aptitude without viewing the answer.
Create one new example and solve it using the lesson method.
Review one distractor or error and explain why it is wrong.
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: Complete an eight-item National Aptitude Championship checkpoint focused on quantitative aptitude. Target at least six correct and justify every uncertain response.
lessons.student_task: Produce one finished National Aptitude Championship task demonstrating quantitative aptitude and record the reasoning, evidence or performance criteria used.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Coach the learner toward evidence-based reasoning and precise terminology. Ask for the method before giving correction, and turn each error into a reusable rule or practice target. This lesson remains suitable for self-learning.
lessons.reflection_completion: Record one strength, one mistake pattern and one concrete action for improving quantitative aptitude in the next practice session.
lessons.daily_flow: Learn → Worked Example → Guided Practice → Independent Practice → Check → Reflect
